literal: Like those who leap into the water knowing it will carry them away, what is the use of sulking, knowing it will prove false?
translation: Like those who plunge into a rushing flood knowing it will sweep them away, what is the use of my sulking when I know it will dissolve the moment we meet?
modern: வெள்ளம் அடித்துச் செல்லும் என்று தெரிந்தே அதில் குதிப்பவர்களைப் போல, என் ஊடல் அவரிடம் தோற்றுப்போகும் என்று தெரிந்தும் நான் ஊடுவதால் என்ன பயன்?
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine compares her feigned anger or sulking to jumping into a swift river. Just as a person leaping into a flood knows they cannot resist the current and will be swept away, she knows her resolve to remain angry will instantly dissolve when her lover approaches. The word 'uyttal' refers to being carried away by the water, and 'poyttal' refers to her sulking proving false or failing to hold up. Thus, she questions the utility ('eṉ') of sulking when she knows she will inevitably yield to love.
